claims.text: Molecular dynamics simulation can be used to produce noble metal-based high-entropy alloy three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
Molecular dynamics simulation can provide precise atomic control in NM-HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
The proposed molecular dynamics simulations use simulation times of 10–100 ns.
The proposed molecular dynamics simulations use temperatures of 300–1000 K.
The proposed molecular dynamics simulations use system sizes of 10–100 nm.
Computational models can predict the behavior of atoms in NM-HEAs.
Predicted atomic behavior can be used to design optimal NM-HEA synthesis conditions.
Predicted atomic behavior can enable precise control over NM-HEA atomic arrangements.
Current methods make NM-HEA formation challenging.
Current methods lack precise atomic control over NM-HEAs.
The proposed approach is limited by molecular dynamics simulation parameters.
The proposed approach is limited by simulated system size.
The accuracy of the computational models is uncertain.
The transferability of simulation results to experimental conditions is uncertain.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and outcome treat molecular dynamics simulation as a method that directly produces physical nanoframeworks, whereas the mediator and mechanism describe it only as a computational prediction and synthesis-design tool. No physical synthesis step connects simulation to production.

The falsification experiment calls for frameworks 'produced using Molecular Dynamics Simulation,' but simulation alone generates computational structures rather than an experimentally synthesized comparison material.
